chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Amr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man in whose possession have gathered from the zakat five hundred or six hundred [coins]. Can he buy a person (slave) with it and free him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then he is unjust to another group regarding their rights.' Then he (peace be upon him) remained silent for a while, then said: 'Unless he happens to be a Muslim slave in desperation, so he buys him and frees him.'
ai.seo_question: Can zakat money be used to buy and free a slave?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the general principle that using zakat for manumission (*itq*) is permissible but potentially unjust to other eligible recipients if it depletes the fund. He refines this by introducing a specific exception for a Muslim slave in dire need (*darurah*), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing the rights of the broader community with the urgent liberation of believers. This ruling highlights the pragmatic application of zakat categories to address social welfare and spiritual freedom within the constraints of equitable distribution.
